facts.fact: The paper (European Scientific Journal, September 2020) says 33 of the 47 county governments had automated their revenues, though some only partially and with structured revenue streams still manual.
facts.system: County revenue automation systems (vendor systems, LAIFOMS)

facts.fact: Automation is described as the move from paper receipts to an electronic system for data entry, processing and reporting, with point-of-sale machines in use; counties mostly collect unstructured revenues (markets, parking, cess), and a taxpayer database linked to the national identifier is listed only as a feature of the proposed integrated system.
facts.system: County revenue automation systems (vendor systems, LAIFOMS)

facts.fact: The survey of 24 of 47 counties found most counties cannot host their revenue data, so it is hosted by the vendor, and a majority of counties still use LAIFOMS in parallel instead of a system integrated with IFMIS.
facts.system: County revenue automation systems (vendor systems, LAIFOMS)

facts.fact: The paper says some counties had only partially automated revenue collection with a number of revenue sources, especially structured ones, still manual, and revenue officers resisting automation revert to manual systems.
facts.system: County revenue automation systems (vendor systems, LAIFOMS)

facts.fact: The paper reports counties' service contracts with revenue-system vendors unclear on revenue share and term, vendors hosting county data, no standardisation, and counties 'at the mercy of vendors'; a 2017 CRA/USAID AHADI assessment of 15 county systems found data owned by the vendors.
facts.system: County revenue automation systems (vendor systems, LAIFOMS)

facts.fact: On 7 February 2019 the President directed a multi-agency task force to deliver one Integrated County Revenue Management System (ICRMS) for all 47 counties; the paper reports no delivery by September 2020.
